newsitem.title: GERMANY: BHF-Bank sees 96 profits up about 5 pct.
newsitem.headline: BHF-Bank sees 96 profits up about 5 pct.

text.p: BHF-Bank AG said on Thursday it expected operating profits to grow about five percent in 1996 and was confident earnings growth would at least match that rate in 1997.
Management board member Wulf von Schimmelmann told Reuters Financial Television it was hard to give a specific number, but added: "Let's say five percent would be a good number."
Schimmelmann said the outlook for 1996 was generally favourable and he expected the trend of the first nine months to continue.
BHF-Bank, Germany's seventh-largest listed bank, posted a rise of 6.6 percent in operating profits during the first nine months of this year.
But Schimmelmann, who is responsible for corporate banking, cautioned that the results would very much depend on risk provisioning during the last quarter of this year.
Asked about his outlook for next year, Schimmelmann said the prospects were even brighter as risk provisions were unlikely to increase.
He added "I see the results for 1997 going at at least the same growth rate as this year."
